The channel, the hour and the retry rule are confirmed. What is missing is a credential
that can *prove* where a message lands:

* **`SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`** on the reporting service (scopes `channels:read` and
  `chat:write`, the app invited to `#gtm-engineering`). The job then resolves the
  channel id by name, refuses if the app is not a member, and records the id on every
  receipt. This is the only path that verifies the destination.
* Otherwise, an explicit statement that the existing
  `SLACK_WEEKLY_REPORT_WEBHOOK_URL` posts to `#gtm-engineering`, which activates the
  job with `--destination-basis webhook-declared`. Nothing can check that claim: an
  incoming webhook cannot be introspected, which is why the code will not assume it.

Until one of those exists the job runs on schedule, measures and stores the week, and
sends nothing.

The channel, the hour and the retry rule are confirmed. What is missing is a credential
that can *prove* where a message lands:

* **`SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`** on the reporting service (scopes `channels:read` and
  `chat:write`, the app invited to `#gtm-engineering`). The job then resolves the
  channel id by name, refuses if the app is not a member, and records the id on every
  receipt. This is the only path that verifies the destination.

  `SLACK_WEEKLY_REPORT_WEBHOOK_URL` posts to `#gtm-engineering`, which activates the
  job with `--destination-basis webhook-declared`. Nothing can check that claim: an
  incoming webhook cannot be introspected, which is why the code will not assume it.

Until one of those exists the job runs on schedule, measures and stores the week, and
sends nothing.

The channel, the hour and the retry rule are confirmed. What is missing is a credential
that can *prove* where a message lands:

* **`SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`** on the reporting service (scopes `channels:read` and
  `chat:write`, the app invited to `#gtm-engineering`). The job then resolves the
  channel id by name, refuses if the app is not a member, and records the id on every
  receipt. This is the only path that verifies the destination.
* Otherwise, an explicit statement that the existing
  `SLACK_WEEKLY_REPORT_WEBHOOK_URL` posts to `#gtm-engineering`, which activates the
  job with `--destination-basis webhook-declared`. Nothing can check that claim: an
  incoming webhook cannot be introspected, which is why the code will not assume it.

Until one of those exists the job runs on schedule, measures and stores the week, and
sends nothing.

The channel, the hour and the retry rule are confirmed. What is missing is a credential
that can *prove* where a message lands:

* **`SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`** on the reporting service (scopes `channels:read` and
  `chat:write`, the app invited to `#gtm-engineering`). The job then resolves the
  channel id by name, refuses if the app is not a member, and records the id on every
  receipt. This is the only path that verifies the destination.
* Otherwise, an explicit statement that the existing
  `SLACK_WEEKLY_REPORT_WEBHOOK_URL` posts to `#gtm-engineering`, which activates the
  job with `--destination-basis webhook-declared`. Nothing can check that claim: an
  incoming webhook cannot be introspected, which is why the code will not assume it.

Until one of those exists the job runs on schedule, measures and stores the week, and
sends nothing.

The channel, the hour and the retry rule are confirmed. What is missing is a credential
that can *prove* where a message lands:

* **`SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`** on the reporting service (scopes `channels:read` and
  `chat:write`, the app invited to `#gtm-engineering`). The job then resolves the
  channel id by name, refuses if the app is not a member, and records the id on every
  receipt. This is the only path that verifies the destination.

  `SLACK_WEEKLY_REPORT_WEBHOOK_URL` posts to `#gtm-engineering`, which activates the
  job with `--destination-basis webhook-declared`. Nothing can check that claim: an

Until one of those exists the job runs on schedule, measures and stores the week, and
sends nothing.

The channel, the hour and the retry rule are confirmed. What is missing is a credential
that can *prove* where a message lands:

* **`SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`** on the reporting service (scopes `channels:read` and
  `chat:write`, the app invited to `#gtm-engineering`). The job then resolves the
  channel id by name, refuses if the app is not a member, and records the id on every
  receipt. This is the only path that verifies the destination.
* Otherwise, an explicit statement that the existing
  `SLACK_WEEKLY_REPORT_WEBHOOK_URL` posts to `#gtm-engineering`, which activates the
  job with `--destination-basis webhook-declared`. Nothing can check that claim: an
  incoming webhook cannot be introspected, which is why the code will not assume it.

Until one of those exists the job runs on schedule, measures and stores the week, and
sends nothing.

The channel, the hour and the retry rule are confirmed. What is missing is a credential
that can *prove* where a message lands:

* **`SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`** on the reporting service (scopes `channels:read` and
  `chat:write`, the app invited to `#gtm-engineering`). The job then resolves the
  channel id by name, refuses if the app is not a member, and records the id on every
  receipt. This is the only path that verifies the destination.
* Otherwise, an explicit statement that the existing
  `SLACK_WEEKLY_REPORT_WEBHOOK_URL` posts to `#gtm-engineering`, which activates the
  job with `--destination-basis webhook-declared`. Nothing can check that claim: an
  incoming webhook cannot be introspected, which is why the code will not assume it.

Until one of those exists the job runs on schedule, measures and stores the week, and
sends nothing.

The channel, the hour and the retry rule are confirmed. What is missing is a credential
that can *prove* where a message lands:

* **`SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`** on the reporting service (scopes `channels:read` and
  `chat:write`, the app invited to `#gtm-engineering`). The job then resolves the
  channel id by name, refuses if the app is not a member, and records the id on every
  receipt. This is the only path that verifies the destination.
* Otherwise, an explicit statement that the existing
  `SLACK_WEEKLY_REPORT_WEBHOOK_URL` posts to `#gtm-engineering`, which activates the
  job with `--destination-basis webhook-declared`. Nothing can check that claim: an
  incoming webhook cannot be introspected, which is why the code will not assume it.

Until one of those exists the job runs on schedule, measures and stores the week, and
sends nothing.

The channel, the hour and the retry rule are confirmed. What is missing is a credential
that can *prove* where a message lands:

* **`SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`** on the reporting service (scopes `channels:read` and
  `chat:write`, the app invited to `#gtm-engineering`). The job then resolves the
  channel id by name, refuses if the app is not a member, and records the id on every
  receipt. This is the only path that verifies the destination.
* Otherwise, an explicit statement that the existing
  `SLACK_WEEKLY_REPORT_WEBHOOK_URL` posts to `#gtm-engineering`, which activates the
  job with `--destination-basis webhook-declared`. Nothing can check that claim: an
  incoming webhook cannot be introspected, which is why the code will not assume it.

Until one of those exists the job runs on schedule, measures and stores the week, and
sends nothing.

The channel, the hour and the retry rule are confirmed. What is missing is a credential
that can *prove* where a message lands:

* **`SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`** on the reporting service (scopes `channels:read` and
  `chat:write`, the app invited to `#gtm-engineering`). The job then resolves the
  channel id by name, refuses if the app is not a member, and records the id on every
  receipt. This is the only path that verifies the destination.
* Otherwise, an explicit statement that the existing
  `SLACK_WEEKLY_REPORT_WEBHOOK_URL` posts to `#gtm-engineering`, which activates the
  job with `--destination-basis webhook-declared`. Nothing can check that claim: an
  incoming webhook cannot be introspected, which is why the code will not assume it.

Until one of those exists the job runs on schedule, measures and stores the week, and
sends nothing.

The channel, the hour and the retry rule are confirmed. What is missing is a credential
that can *prove* where a message lands:

* **`SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`** on the reporting service (scopes `channels:read` and
  `chat:write`, the app invited to `#gtm-engineering`). The job then resolves the
  channel id by name, refuses if the app is not a member, and records the id on every
  receipt. This is the only path that verifies the destination.
* Otherwise, an explicit statement that the existing
  `SLACK_WEEKLY_REPORT_WEBHOOK_URL` posts to `#gtm-engineering`, which activates the
  job with `--destination-basis webhook-declared`. Nothing can check that claim: an
  incoming webhook cannot be introspected, which is why the code will not assume it.

Until one of those exists the job runs on schedule, measures and stores the week, and
sends nothing.

The channel, the hour and the retry rule are confirmed. What is missing is a credential
that can *prove* where a message lands:

* **`SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`** on the reporting service (scopes `channels:read` and
  `chat:write`, the app invited to `#gtm-engineering`). The job then resolves the
  channel id by name, refuses if the app is not a member, and records the id on every
  receipt. This is the only path that verifies the destination.
* Otherwise, an explicit statement that the existing
  `SLACK_WEEKLY_REPORT_WEBHOOK_URL` posts to `#gtm-engineering`, which activates the
  job with `--destination-basis webhook-declared`. Nothing can check that claim: an
  incoming webhook cannot be introspected, which is why the code will not assume it.

Until one of those exists the job runs on schedule, measures and stores the week, and
sends nothing.

The channel, the hour and the retry rule are confirmed. What is missing is a credential
that can *prove* where a message lands:

* **`SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`** on the reporting service (scopes `channels:read` and
  `chat:write`, the app invited to `#gtm-engineering`). The job then resolves the
  channel id by name, refuses if the app is not a member, and records the id on every
  receipt. This is the only path that verifies the destination.
* Otherwise, an explicit statement that the existing
  `SLACK_WEEKLY_REPORT_WEBHOOK_URL` posts to `#gtm-engineering`, which activates the
  job with `--destination-basis webhook-declared`. Nothing can check that claim: an
  incoming webhook cannot be introspected, which is why the code will not assume it.

Until one of those exists the job runs on schedule, measures and stores the week, and
sends nothing.

The channel, the hour and the retry rule are confirmed. What is missing is a credential
that can *prove* where a message lands:

* **`SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`** on the reporting service (scopes `channels:read` and
  `chat:write`, the app invited to `#gtm-engineering`). The job then resolves the
  channel id by name, refuses if the app is not a member, and records the id on every
  receipt. This is the only path that verifies the destination.
* Otherwise, an explicit statement that the existing
  `SLACK_WEEKLY_REPORT_WEBHOOK_URL` posts to `#gtm-engineering`, which activates the
  job with `--destination-basis webhook-declared`. Nothing can check that claim: an
  incoming webhook cannot be introspected, which is why the code will not assume it.

Until one of those exists the job runs on schedule, measures and stores the week, and
sends nothing.

The channel, the hour and the retry rule are confirmed. What is missing is a credential
that can *prove* where a message lands:

* **`SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`** on the reporting service (scopes `channels:read` and
  `chat:write`, the app invited to `#gtm-engineering`). The job then resolves the
  channel id by name, refuses if the app is not a member, and records the id on every
  receipt. This is the only path that verifies the destination.
* Otherwise, an explicit statement that the existing
  `SLACK_WEEKLY_REPORT_WEBHOOK_URL` posts to `#gtm-engineering`, which activates the
  job with `--destination-basis webhook-declared`. Nothing can check that claim: an
  incoming webhook cannot be introspected, which is why the code will not assume it.

Until one of those exists the job runs on schedule, measures and stores the week, and
sends nothing.

The channel, the hour and the retry rule are confirmed. What is missing is a credential
that can *prove* where a message lands:

* **`SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`** on the reporting service (scopes `channels:read` and
  `chat:write`, the app invited to `#gtm-engineering`). The job then resolves the
  channel id by name, refuses if the app is not a member, and records the id on every
  receipt. This is the only path that verifies the destination.
* Otherwise, an explicit statement that the existing
  `SLACK_WEEKLY_REPORT_WEBHOOK_URL` posts to `#gtm-engineering`, which activates the
  job with `--destination-basis webhook-declared`. Nothing can check that claim: an
  incoming webhook cannot be introspected, which is why the code will not assume it.

Until one of those exists the job runs on schedule, measures and stores the week, and
sends nothing.

The channel, the hour and the retry rule are confirmed. What is missing is a credential
that can *prove* where a message lands:

* **`SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`** on the reporting service (scopes `channels:read` and
  `chat:write`, the app invited to `#gtm-engineering`). The job then resolves the
  channel id by name, refuses if the app is not a member, and records the id on every
  receipt. This is the only path that verifies the destination.
* Otherwise, an explicit statement that the existing
  `SLACK_WEEKLY_REPORT_WEBHOOK_URL` posts to `#gtm-engineering`, which activates the
  job with `--destination-basis webhook-declared`. Nothing can check that claim: an
  incoming webhook cannot be introspected, which is why the code will not assume it.

Until one of those exists the job runs on schedule, measures and stores the week, and
sends nothing.

The channel, the hour and the retry rule are confirmed. What is missing is a credential
that can *prove* where a message lands:

* **`SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`** on the reporting service (scopes `channels:read` and
  `chat:write`, the app invited to `#gtm-engineering`). The job then resolves the
  channel id by name, refuses if the app is not a member, and records the id on every
  receipt. This is the only path that verifies the destination.
* Otherwise, an explicit statement that the existing
  `SLACK_WEEKLY_REPORT_WEBHOOK_URL` posts to `#gtm-engineering`, which activates the
  job with `--destination-basis webhook-declared`. Nothing can check that claim: an
  incoming webhook cannot be introspected, which is why the code will not assume it.

Until one of those exists the job runs on schedule, measures and stores the week, and
sends nothing.

The channel, the hour and the retry rule are confirmed. What is missing is a credential
that can *prove* where a message lands:

* **`SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`** on the reporting service (scopes `channels:read` and
  `chat:write`, the app invited to `#gtm-engineering`). The job then resolves the
  channel id by name, refuses if the app is not a member, and records the id on every
  receipt. This is the only path that verifies the destination.
* Otherwise, an explicit statement that the existing
  `SLACK_WEEKLY_REPORT_WEBHOOK_URL` posts to `#gtm-engineering`, which activates the
  job with `--destination-basis webhook-declared`. Nothing can check that claim: an
  incoming webhook cannot be introspected, which is why the code will not assume it.

Until one of those exists the job runs on schedule, measures and stores the week, and
sends nothing.

The channel, the hour and the retry rule are confirmed. What is missing is a credential
that can *prove* where a message lands:

* **`SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`** on the reporting service (scopes `channels:read` and
  `chat:write`, the app invited to `#gtm-engineering`). The job then resolves the
  channel id by name, refuses if the app is not a member, and records the id on every
  receipt. This is the only path that verifies the destination.
* Otherwise, an explicit statement that the existing
  `SLACK_WEEKLY_REPORT_WEBHOOK_URL` posts to `#gtm-engineering`, which activates the
  job with `--destination-basis webhook-declared`. Nothing can check that claim: an
  incoming webhook cannot be introspected, which is why the code will not assume it.

Until one of those exists the job runs on schedule, measures and stores the week, and
sends nothing.

The channel, the hour and the retry rule are confirmed. What is missing is a credential
that can *prove* where a message lands:

* **`SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`** on the reporting service (scopes `channels:read` and
  `chat:write`, the app invited to `#gtm-engineering`). The job then resolves the
  channel id by name, refuses if the app is not a member, and records the id on every
  receipt. This is the only path that verifies the destination.
* Otherwise, an explicit statement that the existing
  `SLACK_WEEKLY_REPORT_WEBHOOK_URL` posts to `#gtm-engineering`, which activates the
  job with `--destination-basis webhook-declared`. Nothing can check that claim: an
  incoming webhook cannot be introspected, which is why the code will not assume it.

Until one of those exists the job runs on schedule, measures and stores the week, and
sends nothing.

The channel, the hour and the retry rule are confirmed. What is missing is a credential
that can *prove* where a message lands:

* **`SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`** on the reporting service (scopes `channels:read` and
  `chat:write`, the app invited to `#gtm-engineering`). The job then resolves the
  channel id by name, refuses if the app is not a member, and records the id on every
  receipt. This is the only path that verifies the destination.
* Otherwise, an explicit statement that the existing
  `SLACK_WEEKLY_REPORT_WEBHOOK_URL` posts to `#gtm-engineering`, which activates the
  job with `--destination-basis webhook-declared`. Nothing can check that claim: an
  incoming webhook cannot be introspected, which is why the code will not assume it.

Until one of those exists the job runs on schedule, measures and stores the week, and
sends nothing.

The channel, the hour and the retry rule are confirmed. What is missing is a credential
that can *prove* where a message lands:

* **`SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`** on the reporting service (scopes `channels:read` and
  `chat:write`, the app invited to `#gtm-engineering`). The job then resolves the
  channel id by name, refuses if the app is not a member, and records the id on every
  receipt. This is the only path that verifies the destination.
* Otherwise, an explicit statement that the existing
  `SLACK_WEEKLY_REPORT_WEBHOOK_URL` posts to `#gtm-engineering`, which activates the
  job with `--destination-basis webhook-declared`. Nothing can check that claim: an
  incoming webhook cannot be introspected, which is why the code will not assume it.

Until one of those exists the job runs on schedule, measures and stores the week, and
sends nothing.

The channel, the hour and the retry rule are confirmed. What is missing is a credential
that can *prove* where a message lands:

* **`SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`** on the reporting service (scopes `channels:read` and
  `chat:write`, the app invited to `#gtm-engineering`). The job then resolves the
  channel id by name, refuses if the app is not a member, and records the id on every
  receipt. This is the only path that verifies the destination.
* Otherwise, an explicit statement that the existing
  `SLACK_WEEKLY_REPORT_WEBHOOK_URL` posts to `#gtm-engineering`, which activates the
  job with `--destination-basis webhook-declared`. Nothing can check that claim: an
  incoming webhook cannot be introspected, which is why the code will not assume it.

Until one of those exists the job runs on schedule, measures and stores the week, and
sends nothing.

that can *prove* where a message lands:

* **`SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`** on the reporting service (scopes `channels:read` and
  `chat:write`, the app invited to `#gtm-engineering`). The job then resolves the
  channel id by name, refuses if the app is not a member, and records the id on every
  receipt. This is the only path that verifies the destination.
* Otherwise, an explicit statement that the existing
  `SLACK_WEEKLY_REPORT_WEBHOOK_URL` posts to `#gtm-engineering`, which activates the
  job with `--destination-basis webhook-declared`. Nothing can check that claim: an
  incoming webhook cannot be introspected, which is why the code will not assume it.

Until one of those exists the job runs on schedule, measures and stores the week, and
sends nothing.

that can *prove* where a message lands:

* **`SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`** on the reporting service (scopes `channels:read` and
  `chat:write`, the app invited to `#gtm-engineering`). The job then resolves the
  channel id by name, refuses if the app is not a member, and records the id on every
  receipt. This is the only path that verifies the destination.
* Otherwise, an explicit statement that the existing
  `SLACK_WEEKLY_REPORT_WEBHOOK_URL` posts to `#gtm-engineering`, which activates the
  job with `--destination-basis webhook-declared`. Nothing can check that claim: an
  incoming webhook cannot be introspected, which is why the code will not assume it.

Until one of those exists the job runs on schedule, measures and stores the week, and
sends nothing.

that can *prove* where a message lands:

* **`SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`** on the reporting service (scopes `channels:read` and
  `chat:write`, the app invited to `#gtm-engineering`). The job then resolves the
  channel id by name, refuses if the app is not a member, and records the id on every
  receipt. This is the only path that verifies the destination.
* Otherwise, an explicit statement that the existing
  `SLACK_WEEKLY_REPORT_WEBHOOK_URL` posts to `#gtm-engineering`, which activates the
  job with `--destination-basis webhook-declared`. Nothing can check that claim: an
  incoming webhook cannot be introspected, which is why the code will not assume it.

Until one of those exists the job runs on schedule, measures and stores the week, and
sends nothing.

that can *prove* where a message lands:

* **`SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`** on the reporting service (scopes `channels:read` and
  `chat:write`, the app invited to `#gtm-engineering`). The job then resolves the
  channel id by name, refuses if the app is not a member, and records the id on every
  receipt. This is the only path that verifies the destination.
* Otherwise, an explicit statement that the existing
  `SLACK_WEEKLY_REPORT_WEBHOOK_URL` posts to `#gtm-engineering`, which activates the
  job with `--destination-basis webhook-declared`. Nothing can check that claim: an
  incoming webhook cannot be introspected, which is why the code will not assume it.

Until one of those exists the job runs on schedule, measures and stores the week, and
sends nothing.

that can *prove* where a message lands:

* **`SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`** on the reporting service (scopes `channels:read` and
  `chat:write`, the app invited to `#gtm-engineering`). The job then resolves the
  channel id by name, refuses if the app is not a member, and records the id on every
  receipt. This is the only path that verifies the destination.
* Otherwise, an explicit statement that the existing
  `SLACK_WEEKLY_REPORT_WEBHOOK_URL` posts to `#gtm-engineering`, which activates the
  job with `--destination-basis webhook-declared`. Nothing can check that claim: an
  incoming webhook cannot be introspected, which is why the code will not assume it.

Until one of those exists the job runs on schedule, measures and stores the week, and
sends nothing.

that can *prove* where a message lands:

* **`SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`** on the reporting service (scopes `channels:read` and
  `chat:write`, the app invited to `#gtm-engineering`). The job then resolves the
  channel id by name, refuses if the app is not a member, and records the id on every
  receipt. This is the only path that verifies the destination.
* Otherwise, an explicit statement that the existing
  `SLACK_WEEKLY_REPORT_WEBHOOK_URL` posts to `#gtm-engineering`, which activates the
  job with `--destination-basis webhook-declared`. Nothing can check that claim: an
  incoming webhook cannot be introspected, which is why the code will not assume it.

Until one of those exists the job runs on schedule, measures and stores the week, and
sends nothing.

that can *prove* where a message lands:

* **`SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`** on the reporting service (scopes `channels:read` and
  `chat:write`, the app invited to `#gtm-engineering`). The job then resolves the
  channel id by name, refuses if the app is not a member, and records the id on every
  receipt. This is the only path that verifies the destination.
* Otherwise, an explicit statement that the existing
  `SLACK_WEEKLY_REPORT_WEBHOOK_URL` posts to `#gtm-engineering`, which activates the
  job with `--destination-basis webhook-declared`. Nothing can check that claim: an
  incoming webhook cannot be introspected, which is why the code will not assume it.

Until one of those exists the job runs on schedule, measures and stores the week, and
sends nothing.

The channel, the hour and the retry rule are confirmed. What is missing is a credential
that can *prove* where a message lands:

* **`SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`** on the reporting service (scopes `channels:read` and
  `chat:write`, the app invited to `#gtm-engineering`). The job then resolves the
  channel id by name, refuses if the app is not a member, and records the id on every
  receipt. This is the only path that verifies the destination.
* Otherwise, an explicit statement that the existing
  `SLACK_WEEKLY_REPORT_WEBHOOK_URL` posts to `#gtm-engineering`, which activates the
  job with `--destination-basis webhook-declared`. Nothing can check that claim: an
  incoming webhook cannot be introspected, which is why the code will not assume it.

Until one of those exists the job runs on schedule, measures and stores the week, and
sends nothing.

The channel, the hour and the retry rule are confirmed. What is missing is a credential
that can *prove* where a message lands:

* **`SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`** on the reporting service (scopes `channels:read` and
  `chat:write`, the app invited to `#gtm-engineering`). The job then resolves the
  channel id by name, refuses if the app is not a member, and records the id on every
  receipt. This is the only path that verifies the destination.
* Otherwise, an explicit statement that the existing
  `SLACK_WEEKLY_REPORT_WEBHOOK_URL` posts to `#gtm-engineering`, which activates the
  job with `--destination-basis webhook-declared`. Nothing can check that claim: an
  incoming webhook cannot be introspected, which is why the code will not assume it.

Until one of those exists the job runs on schedule, measures and stores the week, and
sends nothing.

The channel, the hour and the retry rule are confirmed. What is missing is a credential
that can *prove* where a message lands:

* **`SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`** on the reporting service (scopes `channels:read` and
  `chat:write`, the app invited to `#gtm-engineering`). The job then resolves the
  channel id by name, refuses if the app is not a member, and records the id on every
  receipt. This is the only path that verifies the destination.
* Otherwise, an explicit statement that the existing
  `SLACK_WEEKLY_REPORT_WEBHOOK_URL` posts to `#gtm-engineering`, which activates the
  job with `--destination-basis webhook-declared`. Nothing can check that claim: an
  incoming webhook cannot be introspected, which is why the code will not assume it.

Until one of those exists the job runs on schedule, measures and stores the week, and
sends nothing.

The channel, the hour and the retry rule are confirmed. What is missing is a credential
that can *prove* where a message lands:

* **`SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`** on the reporting service (scopes `channels:read` and
  `chat:write`, the app invited to `#gtm-engineering`). The job then resolves the
  channel id by name, refuses if the app is not a member, and records the id on every
  receipt. This is the only path that verifies the destination.
* Otherwise, an explicit statement that the existing
  `SLACK_WEEKLY_REPORT_WEBHOOK_URL` posts to `#gtm-engineering`, which activates the
  job with `--destination-basis webhook-declared`. Nothing can check that claim: an
  incoming webhook cannot be introspected, which is why the code will not assume it.

Until one of those exists the job runs on schedule, measures and stores the week, and
sends nothing.

The channel, the hour and the retry rule are confirmed. What is missing is a credential
that can *prove* where a message lands:

* **`SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`** on the reporting service (scopes `channels:read` and
  `chat:write`, the app invited to `#gtm-engineering`). The job then resolves the
  channel id by name, refuses if the app is not a member, and records the id on every
  receipt. This is the only path that verifies the destination.
* Otherwise, an explicit statement that the existing
  `SLACK_WEEKLY_REPORT_WEBHOOK_URL` posts to `#gtm-engineering`, which activates the
  job with `--destination-basis webhook-declared`. Nothing can check that claim: an
  incoming webhook cannot be introspected, which is why the code will not assume it.

Until one of those exists the job runs on schedule, measures and stores the week, and
sends nothing.

The channel, the hour and the retry rule are confirmed. What is missing is a credential
that can *prove* where a message lands:

* **`SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`** on the reporting service (scopes `channels:read` and
  `chat:write`, the app invited to `#gtm-engineering`). The job then resolves the
  channel id by name, refuses if the app is not a member, and records the id on every
  receipt. This is the only path that verifies the destination.
* Otherwise, an explicit statement that the existing
  `SLACK_WEEKLY_REPORT_WEBHOOK_URL` posts to `#gtm-engineering`, which activates the
  job with `--destination-basis webhook-declared`. Nothing can check that claim: an
  incoming webhook cannot be introspected, which is why the code will not assume it.

Until one of those exists the job runs on schedule, measures and stores the week, and
sends nothing.

The channel, the hour and the retry rule are confirmed. What is missing is a credential
that can *prove* where a message lands:

* **`SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`** on the reporting service (scopes `channels:read` and
  `chat:write`, the app invited to `#gtm-engineering`). The job then resolves the
  channel id by name, refuses if the app is not a member, and records the id on every
  receipt. This is the only path that verifies the destination.
* Otherwise, an explicit statement that the existing
  `SLACK_WEEKLY_REPORT_WEBHOOK_URL` posts to `#gtm-engineering`, which activates the
  job with `--destination-basis webhook-declared`. Nothing can check that claim: an
  incoming webhook cannot be introspected, which is why the code will not assume it.

Until one of those exists the job runs on schedule, measures and stores the week, and
sends nothing.

The channel, the hour and the retry rule are confirmed. What is missing is a credential
that can *prove* where a message lands:

* **`SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`** on the reporting service (scopes `channels:read` and
  `chat:write`, the app invited to `#gtm-engineering`). The job then resolves the
  channel id by name, refuses if the app is not a member, and records the id on every
  receipt. This is the only path that verifies the destination.
* Otherwise, an explicit statement that the existing
  `SLACK_WEEKLY_REPORT_WEBHOOK_URL` posts to `#gtm-engineering`, which activates the
  job with `--destination-basis webhook-declared`. Nothing can check that claim: an
  incoming webhook cannot be introspected, which is why the code will not assume it.

Until one of those exists the job runs on schedule, measures and stores the week, and
sends nothing.

The channel, the hour and the retry rule are confirmed. What is missing is a credential
that can *prove* where a message lands:

* **`SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`** on the reporting service (scopes `channels:read` and
  `chat:write`, the app invited to `#gtm-engineering`). The job then resolves the
  channel id by name, refuses if the app is not a member, and records the id on every
  receipt. This is the only path that verifies the destination.
* Otherwise, an explicit statement that the existing
  `SLACK_WEEKLY_REPORT_WEBHOOK_URL` posts to `#gtm-engineering`, which activates the
  job with `--destination-basis webhook-declared`. Nothing can check that claim: an
  incoming webhook cannot be introspected, which is why the code will not assume it.

Until one of those exists the job runs on schedule, measures and stores the week, and
sends nothing.

The channel, the hour and the retry rule are confirmed. What is missing is a credential
that can *prove* where a message lands:

* **`SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`** on the reporting service (scopes `channels:read` and
  `chat:write`, the app invited to `#gtm-engineering`). The job then resolves the
  channel id by name, refuses if the app is not a member, and records the id on every
  receipt. This is the only path that verifies the destination.
* Otherwise, an explicit statement that the existing
  `SLACK_WEEKLY_REPORT_WEBHOOK_URL` posts to `#gtm-engineering`, which activates the
  job with `--destination-basis webhook-declared`. Nothing can check that claim: an
  incoming webhook cannot be introspected, which is why the code will not assume it.

Until one of those exists the job runs on schedule, measures and stores the week, and
sends nothing.

The channel, the hour and the retry rule are confirmed. What is missing is a credential
that can *prove* where a message lands:

* **`SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`** on the reporting service (scopes `channels:read` and
  `chat:write`, the app invited to `#gtm-engineering`). The job then resolves the
  channel id by name, refuses if the app is not a member, and records the id on every
  receipt. This is the only path that verifies the destination.
* Otherwise, an explicit statement that the existing
  `SLACK_WEEKLY_REPORT_WEBHOOK_URL` posts to `#gtm-engineering`, which activates the
  job with `--destination-basis webhook-declared`. Nothing can check that claim: an
  incoming webhook cannot be introspected, which is why the code will not assume it.

Until one of those exists the job runs on schedule, measures and stores the week, and
sends nothing.

The channel, the hour and the retry rule are confirmed. What is missing is a credential
that can *prove* where a message lands:

* **`SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`** on the reporting service (scopes `channels:read` and
  `chat:write`, the app invited to `#gtm-engineering`). The job then resolves the
  channel id by name, refuses if the app is not a member, and records the id on every
  receipt. This is the only path that verifies the destination.
* Otherwise, an explicit statement that the existing
  `SLACK_WEEKLY_REPORT_WEBHOOK_URL` posts to `#gtm-engineering`, which activates the
  job with `--destination-basis webhook-declared`. Nothing can check that claim: an
  incoming webhook cannot be introspected, which is why the code will not assume it.

Until one of those exists the job runs on schedule, measures and stores the week, and
sends nothing.

The channel, the hour and the retry rule are confirmed. What is missing is a credential
that can *prove* where a message lands:

* **`SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`** on the reporting service (scopes `channels:read` and
  `chat:write`, the app invited to `#gtm-engineering`). The job then resolves the
  channel id by name, refuses if the app is not a member, and records the id on every
  receipt. This is the only path that verifies the destination.
* Otherwise, an explicit statement that the existing
  `SLACK_WEEKLY_REPORT_WEBHOOK_URL` posts to `#gtm-engineering`, which activates the
  job with `--destination-basis webhook-declared`. Nothing can check that claim: an
  incoming webhook cannot be introspected, which is why the code will not assume it.

Until one of those exists the job runs on schedule, measures and stores the week, and
sends nothing.

The channel, the hour and the retry rule are confirmed. What is missing is a credential
that can *prove* where a message lands:

* **`SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`** on the reporting service (scopes `channels:read` and
  `chat:write`, the app invited to `#gtm-engineering`). The job then resolves the
  channel id by name, refuses if the app is not a member, and records the id on every
  receipt. This is the only path that verifies the destination.
* Otherwise, an explicit statement that the existing
  `SLACK_WEEKLY_REPORT_WEBHOOK_URL` posts to `#gtm-engineering`, which activates the
  job with `--destination-basis webhook-declared`. Nothing can check that claim: an
  incoming webhook cannot be introspected, which is why the code will not assume it.

Until one of those exists the job runs on schedule, measures and stores the week, and
sends nothing.

The channel, the hour and the retry rule are confirmed. What is missing is a credential
that can *prove* where a message lands:

* **`SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`** on the reporting service (scopes `channels:read` and
  `chat:write`, the app invited to `#gtm-engineering`). The job then resolves the
  channel id by name, refuses if the app is not a member, and records the id on every
  receipt. This is the only path that verifies the destination.
* Otherwise, an explicit statement that the existing
  `SLACK_WEEKLY_REPORT_WEBHOOK_URL` posts to `#gtm-engineering`, which activates the
  job with `--destination-basis webhook-declared`. Nothing can check that claim: an
  incoming webhook cannot be introspected, which is why the code will not assume it.

Until one of those exists the job runs on schedule, measures and stores the week, and
sends nothing.

The channel, the hour and the retry rule are confirmed. What is missing is a credential
that can *prove* where a message lands:

* **`SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`** on the reporting service (scopes `channels:read` and
  `chat:write`, the app invited to `#gtm-engineering`). The job then resolves the
  channel id by name, refuses if the app is not a member, and records the id on every
  receipt. This is the only path that verifies the destination.
* Otherwise, an explicit statement that the existing
  `SLACK_WEEKLY_REPORT_WEBHOOK_URL` posts to `#gtm-engineering`, which activates the
  job with `--destination-basis webhook-declared`. Nothing can check that claim: an
  incoming webhook cannot be introspected, which is why the code will not assume it.

Until one of those exists the job runs on schedule, measures and stores the week, and
sends nothing.
